finding.claim: SQL injection via unsanitized ORDER BY clause: the `sort` GET parameter is concatenated directly into the query string in list_users_sorted().
finding.source: HTTP GET parameter `sort` ($_GET['sort']) at list.php:5, supplied by any unauthenticated remote client

trace.note: string concatenated into 'SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY ' . $sort and executed via PDO::query

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, cast, or parameter binding on this path (ORDER BY cannot be parameterized anyway). The sibling list_users_safe() at line 10-12 uses an allowlist map, showing the intended control is missing here. No authentication or other middleware exists in the repo. In SQLite, attacker can use e.g. a CASE/subquery in ORDER BY for boolean blind extraction of any table data (e.g. other tables or user columns).

verdict.guard_found: none on list_users_sorted(); the allowlist at list.php:10-11 only protects list_users_safe()
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (list.php:5 reads $_GET['sort'] and list.php:6 concatenates it into PDO::query with no guard), but list.php only defines list_users_sorted() and never calls it, and no other file exists, so I can't confirm it is reachable by a remote attacker.
